title: Marriages Are Largely Happening in Middle America and Not in Urban Centers, Study Finds | Institute for Family Studies
gist: A new IFS study finds the largest share of unmarried young adults sits in urban centers like Cleveland, Detroit, Philadelphia, Chicago, and Washington, D.C., while the areas producing the most new marriages are almost entirely in middle America—Provo, Fort Wayne, Evansville, Colorado Springs, and parts of Tennessee, Georgia, and North Carolina—even as the national marriage rate hovers near its all-time low.

insights.claim: A new IFS study finds the areas with the most new marriages are almost entirely in middle America, including Provo, Utah; Fort Wayne and Evansville, Indiana; Colorado Springs, Colorado; plus west/central Tennessee, northwest Georgia, and North Carolina's Greenville/Jacksonville corridor.
insights.speaker: Dan Hart
insights.so_what: Marriage-driven household formation concentrates in interior metros, marking where family-linked housing and consumer demand is structurally strongest.
insights.quote: The areas with the most new marriages are almost entirely in middle America
insights.locator: The report, published by the Institute for Family Studies

insights.claim: The largest share of unmarried young adults in their 20s and 30s is in urban centers like Cleveland, Detroit, Philadelphia, Chicago, and Washington, D.C.
insights.speaker: Dan Hart
insights.so_what: Big coastal and rust-belt cities skew toward singles, a demographic split that shapes divergent regional housing and lifestyle markets.
insights.quote: the largest share of unmarried young adults in their 20s and 30s are in urban centers like Cleveland, Detroit, Philadelphia, Chicago, and Washington, D.C.
insights.locator: The report, published by the Institute for Family Studies

insights.claim: The US marriage rate is still hovering near an all-time low reached in 2019, even though polls consistently show the desire for marriage remains strong among young adults.
insights.speaker: Dan Hart
insights.so_what: A gap between strong marriage desire and near-record-low marriage rates signals unmet demand that policy or market shifts could unlock.
insights.quote: the marriage rate in America still hovering near an all-time low reached in 2019, despite polls consistently showing that the desire for marriage remains strong for young adults
insights.locator: With the marriage rate in America
